skills.trigger: When evaluating diffuse pulmonary nodules on chest CT to determine the underlying etiology based on distribution pattern.
steps: Assess the spatial relationship of nodules to secondary pulmonary lobule structures: check if they cluster around bronchovascular bundles (peribronchovascular), lie within the centrilobular region sparing the immediate subpleural space, or are distributed randomly throughout the lobule including the subpleura and fissures.

Distinguish peribronchovascular/subpleural distribution (suggestive of sarcoidosis or lymphangitic carcinomatosis) from centrilobular distribution (suggestive of inhalational diseases like hypersensitivity pneumonitis) and random distribution (suggestive of hematogenous spread like miliary TB or metastases).

skills.trigger: When differentiating between granulomatous diseases and other diffuse lung pathologies presenting with nodular opacities.
steps: Identify the presence of well-defined nodules specifically tracking along the peribronchovascular interstitium and subpleural regions (including fissures).

Correlate this specific 'axial' distribution pattern with sarcoidosis, while excluding miliary tuberculosis (which typically shows random distribution) and inhalational diseases (which typically show centrilobular distribution with subpleural sparing).
